sections.html:
East central Alabama holds Elmore County, immediately north of Montgomery and inside that metro area. Wetumpka has the courthouse and Millbrook has the most people. Terrain follows the fall line, moving from rolling hills to open farm fields, and Wetumpka and Tallassee both have river frontage. Say in any description what type of lot the house has.

Elmore is one of Alabama's fastest-growing counties. Residents numbered 49,210 in 1990, 65,874 in 2000, 79,303 in 2010 and 87,977 in 2020, and 91,577 are estimated for 2025. In 2020 the county counted 32,567 households and 36,818 housing units, 11.5 percent of them empty. Three quarters of occupied homes, 76.0 percent, are owner-occupied. Homeowner vacancy is 1.5 percent, rental vacancy 6.5 percent, and about 71 percent of the population lives in rural areas.

Your neighbors might be long-time river-town owners or commuters in newer subdivisions. The Elmore County Public School System covers most addresses, while one portion belongs to the Tallassee City School District. Buyers ask about schools first, so learn which applies before you list or take an offer.

The four cities are Prattville (partly in Autauga County), Millbrook (partly in Autauga County), Tallassee (partly in Tallapoosa County) and Wetumpka. The four towns are Coosada, Deatsville, Eclectic and Elmore, and Blue Ridge, Emerald Mountain, Holtville and Redland are census-designated places.

The county line cuts through several of these places, and that decides where a deed is recorded and who bills the tax. A parcel in the Autauga part of Prattville or Millbrook belongs to a different county than one in Elmore's part. Look at your tax bill before you contact any office.

Elmore voters approved a single Revenue Commissioner on March 6, 1990, under Act No. 90-254, and that office combined the jobs of tax assessor and tax collector. It covers about 44,000 parcels across roughly 630 square miles and also values business personal property and personal aircraft.

Visit 100 E. Commerce Street, Suite 102, in Wetumpka, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or call 334-567-1184. A Citizen Access Portal and a parcel viewer are linked from the county's website, and both are handy for looking up your own record before you sell.

Payment is due on October 1 and the account becomes delinquent after December 31. From then on an unpaid account moves through the same statewide sequence, ending at a probate court sale.

DateStep
October 1Tax due
January 1Delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to the Probate Court
MarchProbate Court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

Interest and penalties are added to past-due balances, so call the Revenue Commissioner for the exact charge on your account.

A mandatory fire fee for volunteer fire services was also approved by voters in the late 1990s. Each citizen pays the same flat amount, regardless of property value or income, so your assessment has no effect on it. Ask the county how the fee is billed to you.

Alabama Code 40-22-1 sets a recording privilege tax of fifty cents on every $500 of value, with the probate recording fee charged separately. The state treasury takes two-thirds of the tax and the county treasury one-third.

You certify the sale price on the Department of Revenue form. Leave out proof of price and the tax may be based on the latest assessment, with a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax if that is larger. Once the sale is done, the buyer records the deed at the probate office, then carries it to the Revenue Commissioner for assessment.

We hear about empty inherited houses in Wetumpka or Tallassee, rentals left vacant by a departing tenant, river houses overdue for repairs, and owners behind on tax with the May sale ahead.

Our cash purchase can settle the tax and take the house untouched, saving the expense of getting it ready for a retail listing.

  1. Read your tax bill to see which county holds the parcel.
  2. Phone the Revenue Commissioner for the balance by year.
  3. Find the deed, plus probate papers for an inherited house.
  4. Have the title company confirm each payoff ahead of closing.

Near the river? Dig out flood paperwork and repair receipts. In a newer subdivision, locate the builder's warranty papers if they still apply. Small items like these settle a buyer's opening questions.

A house nobody lives in is the easiest to lose track of. Bills pile up at the old address, grass grows and neighbors start to wonder. If you inherited a house in Wetumpka or Tallassee, begin with the basics: who is on the deed, which years of tax are open and whether anyone is entitled to a share. Courtesy notices from the Revenue Commissioner may never have reached you, so do not assume a quiet mailbox means a clear account.

Next, secure the property. Change the locks if keys are unaccounted for, check the roof and the water shut-off, and photograph each room. That record protects you if a question comes up later. Keep the utilities on if you can, since buyers walk through with lights on.

Finally, put all the heirs on one conversation. Disagreements about price and timing are common, and a sale needs every signature. Share the tax figures with everyone so the numbers are not a surprise at closing.

After you say yes, a title company or attorney runs the file. Staff there search the title, collect payoff figures from the Revenue Commissioner and any lender, and draft a settlement statement. Read it, sign the deed, and the balance reaches you once taxes, payoffs and recording costs are subtracted.

Plan to bring photo identification and keys. Does your city cross the county line? Then say which side the house is on, so the deed lands at the correct probate office. After closing, the buyer assesses the property with the Revenue Commissioner, so that part is no longer your task. You should still keep your closing papers and the final tax receipt for your records.

Retail sales ask a lot of a seller. You clean, repair, stage, host showings and then wait for a buyer's lender to finish an appraisal. Any of those steps can fall through. A cash sale removes the lender, so the date is set by the title work and your own schedule.

That suits sellers who are moving fast, carrying a second house or looking at a May tax sale. It also suits an owner whose house has deferred repairs, since we take it as is. We will explain exactly how an offer is figured and what comes out at closing, so you can compare it with listing the house and decide for yourself.

If you are not ready to decide, that is fine. Take the tax figures and the deed information we reviewed together, talk to a family member or an attorney, and call back when you are ready.

faqs.q: Who bills and collects property tax in Elmore County?
faqs.a: The Elmore County Revenue Commissioner, whose office combines assessing and collecting. It is at 100 E. Commerce Street, Suite 102, Wetumpka, phone 334-567-1184.

faqs.q: When are Elmore County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1. They become delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Elmore County?
faqs.a: Wetumpka. Millbrook is the largest city.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax on an Elmore County sale?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, plus the probate recording fee.

faqs.q: Is Elmore County part of the Montgomery area?
faqs.a: Yes. It lies just north of Montgomery and belongs to the Montgomery metropolitan area.
